Optional. Web address of update_db_eol_dashboard_dates.py, for example its raw GitHub URL. Leave empty to use the copy next to the template.

### Other database services
- **Azure SQL Managed Instance**: there are no version end dates. Each instance follows an update policy. The SQL Server 2022 update policy is available until SQL Server 2022 mainstream support ends (January 2028), and instances then move automatically to the policy for the latest SQL Server release ([update policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/managed-instance/update-policy?view=azuresql)).
- **Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (RU)**: the dashboard shows each account's server version. Azure has no end-of-support plans for these versions and gives at least three years' notice before ending one ([3.6 server version](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/feature-support-36)), so there's no date to count down to. Versions below the **MongoDB: review versions below** setting are marked *Review* to help plan upgrades for newer features and driver support. The upgrade is done in place from the account's Features page, without downtime; upgrade the application drivers first ([upgrade the server version](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/upgrade-version)).
- **Azure DocumentDB (MongoDB vCore)**: clusters show their MongoDB version and use the same review setting. Upgrade from the cluster's Overview page ([upgrade a cluster](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/documentdb/how-to-upgrade-cluster)).
- **Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra**: clusters show their Cassandra version. Versions below the **Cassandra: review versions below** setting (4.0 by default, so 3.11) are marked *Review*: 3.11 reached community end of life at the end of 2023.
- **Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL**: each cluster's PostgreSQL version is checked against the retirement dates on its supported versions page. The service itself is on a retirement path, so every row suggests planning a move to Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters.
- **Azure Cache for Redis**: the Basic, Standard and Premium tiers retire on 30 September 2028, and the Enterprise and Enterprise Flash tiers on 31 March 2027 ([retirement FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/retirement-faq)). These dates count down like version end dates. Azure Managed Redis is listed with its version and no end date.
- **Retired services**: any Azure Database for PostgreSQL or MySQL single server and Azure Database for MariaDB still listed is shown as past end of support.
- **Azure SQL Database** and **Cosmos DB for NoSQL, Cassandra, Table and Gremlin** have no versions to upgrade, so they're listed as *Not version-based* for a complete inventory. Use the Status filter to hide them. The SQL server that Azure Synapse Analytics creates for each workspace is left out, because Synapse manages it.

### SQL Server enabled by Azure Arc, and SQL Server on Azure VMs
- The dashboard lists the database engine instances that Azure Arc reports (SQL Server 2012 and later), and the Azure VMs registered with the SQL IaaS Agent extension. Reporting Services and other associated services are left out.
- **ESU (SQL Server)**: for Arc-enabled servers it shows the Extended Security Updates setting of the server's SQL Server extension. SQL Server 2014 on Azure VMs gets ESUs free through Windows Update. ESU subscriptions for other Azure VMs, and ESUs bought through volume licensing, aren't visible to the dashboard, so those servers show *Not reported* or *Not subscribed (Azure Arc)*.
- **Owner**: taken from the owner tag on the SQL Server resource, or else from the tag on its Arc-enabled server or VM.
- An instance shown as *Azure Arc (disconnected)* hasn't reported recently, so its details may be out of date.
- Learn more: [Extended Security Updates for SQL Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/sql-server/end-of-support/sql-server-extended-security-updates)

## Using this dashboard
- Review it monthly, and weekly once anything turns Red. Pin the summary tiles to an Azure dashboard to keep them on your home screen.
- Narrow the view with the **Database types**, **Tag name** and **Tag values**, **Resource groups** and **Status** filters at the top of the **Database versions** tab. They apply to the tiles, the resource group summary and both tables. Each list only shows what matches the filters before it.
- **Versions in use** has one row per engine version, most urgent first. Select a row to list just those servers in the table below it, and select **Show all versions** to go back to the full list.
- **Tag filter**: pick a tag name such as *environment*, then the values to show. Tag names and values are matched regardless of case, so they're listed in lower case. For SQL Server, the tag on its Arc-enabled server or VM is used when the SQL Server resource doesn't have the tag. Pick *(not tagged)* to find servers that are missing the tag.
- To find one server, type part of its name, owner or version in the search box above the table.
- **Servers by resource group** lists the groups with the most servers past end of support or Red first, which helps to plan the work by team or application.
- Change the Red and Amber thresholds, the owner tag name, the MongoDB and Cassandra review versions and who gets the reminder emails with the settings at the top of the **Database versions** tab, then save the dashboard.
- Use **Export to Excel** on the table to share the list or attach it to a change request. The filters don't change the reminder emails, which always cover every server.

## Keeping the dates current
- A weekly update job (an Azure Automation runbook) reads Microsoft's version support pages, the SQL Server lifecycle pages and the Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL versions page, checks the dates and saves them here. The banner at the top shows when the dates were last checked, and turns orange if they haven't been checked for 45 days.
- Don't edit the dates in the dashboard by hand, because the next run replaces them. To set a date yourself, add it to *DATE_OVERRIDES* in the runbook's settings.
- Without the update job, the dashboard keeps the dates it was installed with.

## Reminder emails
- The same job emails the addresses in **Reminder emails to** a weekly summary of every Red server and every server already past end of support. Each owner whose email address is in a server's owner tag (default tag name: *Owner*) also gets their own list.
- Services with no deadline (*Review*, *No end date*, *Not version-based*) aren't included in the emails.
- Nothing is sent in a week when no server needs a reminder, or while **Reminder emails to** is empty. The Red threshold and owner tag name set on the **Database versions** tab are used for the emails too, once the dashboard is saved."}, "name": "lifecycle how to use"}]}, "conditionalVisibility": {"parameterName": "selectedTab", "comparison": "isEqualTo", "value": "reference"}, "name": "tab - lifecycle reference"}], "fallbackResourceIds": ["Azure Monitor"], "$schema": "https://github.com/Microsoft/Application-Insights-Workbooks/blob/master/schema/workbook.json"}
